ShortDescription.Value: Per-district line charts of budget history and tax rates. Plus reworked services tab, density taxes and district service budgets.

Publish.LongDescription:
See where your city's money has been going, and run it district by district. Fiscal Overhaul swaps the Budget tab's bar chart for a line chart of your income and expenses over time, turns the Services tab into a clear table of what each service costs and earns, and lets every district set its own tax rates. It also adds density taxes and per-district service budgets.
## Control your city's finances per district! * A **district selector** at the left of the Economy panel's tabs, framed together with **Budget, Taxation and Services**. The options are: Entire City (shown as your city's name), each of your districts, or Outside Districts (everything not in a district). * Step through with the arrows, or click the name to pick from the list. The choice carries across the three tabs.
## Budget tab * **Per-district budgets**: pick a district to see what its buildings pay in taxes, at its own rates, and its share of service fees and upkeep by use. City-wide items (loan interest, map tile upkeep, service trade, subsidies) show under the whole city only. District history is recorded from the first time the mod runs on a save and kept in the save. * **Line chart** of total revenue, total expenses, the monthly balance and any single budget item, each as a per-month rate (the same figure the vanilla panel shows). * **Series filters**: click a row to show or hide its line; ticking a group turns its items on or off together. Only the items your city has are listed. * **Time span** from 1 month to all history (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, All). The city's history is the game's own budget statistics, already kept in your save, so a loaded city shows everything back to its founding. * **Exact values on hover**: the tooltip shows the hovered line's monthly value and how long ago it was, with the span's change and average at the top of the chart. * **Vanilla detail panel**: hovering a budget item pops out the game's own breakdown by source.
## Services tab * **A table like the Taxation tab**: one row per service with its **budget slider** and its **cost** (upkeep and imports), and a row under it for each **fee** with its **revenue**. Electricity and Water fees have their sliders right there. * **Estimated total** at the bottom: the rows add up to it. * **Reset buttons and markers**: each slider shows where its default is, and a button puts it back. * **The game's info column** at the right explains whatever you hover: a service, its budget (with the efficiency it gives) or a fee's effects. * Prefer the vanilla tab? Turn off **Enable services table** in Options.
## Taxation tab * **Per-district tax rates**: pick a district (or Outside Districts) in the header and set its own rates, each zone with its education levels and resources. A district without its own rate follows the city's, and the estimates show what the district brings in. * Demand, happiness and the homes households choose react to a district's rates as to the city's. * **Reset buttons and markers** on every row: a district's row goes back to the city's rate, the city's to the game's default.
## Density taxes **On by default**, with every rate at 0 until you set one; **Enable density taxes** in Options > Fiscal Overhaul turns it off. * A **density tax** per zone and building density (residential low / medium / high, commercial low / high, office low / high, industrial), from −5% to +10%, paid on top of income tax. The city and each district can set their own. * Demand, happiness and households choosing homes react to it as to any tax, and the Taxation tab estimates what each density rate brings in.
## District service budgets **On by default**; no district has its own budget until you set one. **District service budgets** in Options turns it off. * Each district (and Outside Districts) can run a service at its **own budget**, from 50% to 150%, changing that district's service buildings' efficiency and upkeep. Districts without one follow the city slider. * Set them on the Services tab with the district picker; the table then shows that district's costs and fee revenue.
## Options **Features** (change only what you see): * **Enable budget chart** (on): off, the Budget tab is the vanilla one. * **Record district budgets** (on): off, nothing new is recorded; what was recorded is kept. * **Enable services table** (on): off, the Services tab is the vanilla one.
**Simulation changes** (change how the game plays): * **Simulation changes** (on): the master switch. Off, the game charges its own taxes again and every service building follows the city's budget slider; your rates and settings are kept. * **Enable density taxes** and **District service budgets** (both on). * **Run on untested game version** (off): the mod's tax charging is checked against specific game versions; on any other, taxes stay vanilla (a notice at the top of the Options page says so) unless you tick this.
**Reset**: district service budgets, and density tax rates.
## Compatibility * Game version 1.6.x. * Replaces the vanilla Budget and Services pages and extends the Taxation tab and the Economy panel's tab bar: another mod that replaces any of those may conflict. Mods that change how taxes are charged may interact with district and density tax rates. * **Saves**: the mod keeps its district history, district tax rates and district service budgets in your save. Removing the mod is safe: the save still loads, the game skips that data, and taxes and services go back to vanilla.
## Bugs and source Bug reports and suggestions: [GitHub issues](https://github.com/DarrenGKelly/fiscal-overhaul/issues). Source code (MIT): [github.com/DarrenGKelly/fiscal-overhaul](https://github.com/DarrenGKelly/fiscal-overhaul).
## Support If you enjoy the mod and want to say thanks, you can [buy me a coffee on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/darrengkelly). Entirely optional: the mod is and stays free.
Publish.ChangeLog:
### Added
- **One district picker for three tabs:** a picker at the left of the Economy panel's tabs, framed with Budget, Taxation and Services, chooses the city, one district or Outside Districts for all three. Long district names fit. - **Tax rates per district:** each district (and Outside Districts) can set its own zone, education, resource and density rates; a district without its own rate follows the city's. The Taxation tab shows the district's own estimates, and demand, happiness and the homes households choose react to its rates. - **Services tab as a table:** one row per service with its budget slider and its cost, a row for each fee with its revenue, an estimated total, reset buttons and default markers, and the game's info column for whatever you hover. Turn it off with **Enable services table** to get the vanilla tab back. - **District service budgets (BETA, off by default):** a district can run a service at its own budget, from 50% to 150%, changing its buildings' efficiency and upkeep. - **Simulation changes** switch in Options: off, the game charges its own taxes and every service follows the city's slider again, with your rates and settings kept. - Budget tab: collapsible categories, Service Upkeep broken down by service, and group checkboxes that turn a category and all its items on or off together.
### Changed
- Density taxes are now charged as a real tax: they pay the city (a negative rate is booked as a subsidy), and demand, happiness and home choice react to them. Density and district rates are kept in each save. - The Economy tabs are ordered Budget, Taxation, Services, Production, Loans. - Taxation: Education/Resources and Density are collapsible sections, density rows look like the game's own rows, and every row has a reset button and a marker at its default. - The Options page is grouped into Features, Simulation changes and Reset. - The budget chart draws as soon as the tab opens. - New store page screenshots and description.
### Fixed
- Taxation estimates match what the city collects (they read 5-7% high on small incomes), and are right from the first moments after loading a save instead of starting low. - The district list closes when you click outside it or switch tabs.
